replacements.instruction: Remove the benchmark-by-benchmark score recap from Discussion because those results are already reported in Results, while retaining the discussion-level synthesis that direct same-prompt preference is the clearest advantage and the interpretation that process-level control need not maximize every metric.
replacements.before:
Tables~\ref{tab:main-results} and~\ref{tab:pairwise-results} show that the clearest advantage of \condAgenticCogWriter\ is not uniform dominance under every pointwise score, but consistent preference in direct same-prompt comparisons.
The system has the highest displayed means on WritingBench and HelloBench, whereas \condStaged\ has the highest DoLoMiTes pointwise mean without a paired interval separating it from our system; pairwise evaluation favors our system over single-pass generation, fixed writing stages, and adaptive task planning on every benchmark.
The pattern supports process-level control as a useful way to organize long-form generation without requiring it to maximize every benchmark-specific metric.
replacements.after:
Tables~\ref{tab:main-results} and~\ref{tab:pairwise-results} show that the clearest advantage of \condAgenticCogWriter\ is not uniform dominance under every pointwise score, but consistent preference in direct same-prompt comparisons.
The pattern supports process-level control as a useful way to organize long-form generation without requiring it to maximize every benchmark-specific metric.

replacements.instruction: Combine the repeated ablation and execution-diagnostic evidence into one sentence while preserving the near-parity No-goals/Fixed-order result, the larger Single-writer gap, and the fact that the post-hoc Single-context diagnostic does not isolate subagent delegation.
replacements.before:
Removing the goal representation or fixing the process order leaves performance near the full system, whereas the larger \condSingleWriter\ gap points to execution structure as another candidate explanation.
The post-hoc \condSingleContext\ diagnostic, however, does not reduce that difference to subagent delegation alone.
replacements.after: Near-parity results for \condNoGoals\ and \condFixedOrder\ and the larger \condSingleWriter\ gap point to execution structure as another candidate explanation, but the post-hoc \condSingleContext\ diagnostic does not reduce that gap to subagent delegation alone.
